parsed.explanation: No trans-specific criminalisation; constitutional and statutory anti-discrimination covers gender identity (2015) with hate-crime sentence enhancements (2019). Traveller-facing exposures are undocumented: no border, facility, custody or care restrictions appear — these are open questions, not exposures, and the rubric forbids weighing missing resident-facing machinery (court-by-court LGR) against the visitor. Extrapolation rests on structural signals: functioning courts, an active NGO with ministry cooperation, legal Pride in the capital, and a 2019 prosecution of an official calling for violence — rule of law acting against, not for, hostility. Negative signals: documented implementation gaps, underreporting of bias crimes (most incidents never reach police), and recurring political hate speech — social-hostility friction, not organised targeting, with no trans-specific violence data either way. This sits between the 0.55 and 0.65 anchors: real unremedied discrimination and thin recourse, but no universal exclusion or state threat-framing.
